Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The present invention discloses a self-lubricating fabric, a method for producing the self-lubricating fabric, and use of the self-lubricating fabric. Warp yarns or weft yarns of the fabric are composite yarns formed from fluorinated resin yarns and other yarns. The surface area of the other yarns on one surface of the fabric takes up 0 to 30% of the total surface area of the composite yarns, and the ratio of the section diameter of the other yarns to the section diameter of the fluorinated resin yarns in the composite yarns is 0.12 to 0.80. The self-lubricating fabric is characterized by low friction coefficient, excellent wear resistance property and high laminating strength, as well as simple production process, low cost and zero pollution to the environment. The fabric with low friction coefficient can be applied to mechanical moving parts, and is especially suitable for use in environment of low speed, high load and high or low temperature.

The invention relates to a self-lubricating fabric, a method for producing the fabric, and the intended applications of the fabric.

The self-lubricating fabric is formed by using composite yarns in the warp direction, the weft direction, or both. These composite yarns are made from fluorinated resin yarns combined with one or more other types of yarns. The fluorinated resin yarns provide the fabric with excellent self-lubricating properties, while the additional yarns may be selected to improve strength, bonding performance, dimensional stability, or other mechanical properties required for specific applications.

In the fabric structure, the additional yarns are arranged so that they occupy from 0% to 30% of the surface area on one side of the fabric. The ratio of the sectional diameter of the additional yarns to the sectional diameter of the fluorinated resin yarns is controlled within the range of 0.12 to 0.80. By regulating both the exposed surface area and the diameter ratio of the yarns, the fabric achieves an effective balance between lubricating performance and structural strength. The fluorinated resin yarns dominate the sliding surface, thereby ensuring a low coefficient of friction, while the other yarns contribute to improved adhesion and reinforcement.

The production method of the fabric is simple and efficient. It does not require complicated coating, impregnation, or post-treatment processes, and therefore reduces manufacturing cost. In addition, the process avoids pollution problems that may be associated with conventional lubrication or surface-treatment techniques. The resulting fabric has a low friction coefficient, excellent wear resistance, and high laminating strength, making it reliable under demanding operating conditions.

The self-lubricating fabric is particularly suitable for use in mechanical moving parts where friction reduction and long service life are required. It may be applied to sliding bearings, bushings, guide rails, wear-resistant linings, and other frictional components. The fabric is especially advantageous in low-speed and high-load operating environments, where conventional lubricants may be ineffective or difficult to maintain. It is also suitable for use under high-temperature or low-temperature conditions, making it applicable to a wide range of industrial, automotive, aerospace, and mechanical equipment applications.
outputs.L4:
A self-lubricating fabric is produced by weaving composite warp yarns and/or composite weft yarns that include fluorinated resin yarns combined with one or more other types of yarn. The fluorinated resin component provides the fabric with a naturally low coefficient of friction, while the additional yarn component improves structural strength, dimensional stability, adhesion, and wear resistance. By controlling the relative surface-area ratio and diameter ratio between the fluorinated resin yarns and the other yarns, the fabric can achieve an optimized balance between lubrication performance and mechanical durability.

The composite yarns may be prepared by twisting, combining, covering, or otherwise integrating fluorinated resin yarns with reinforcing or bonding yarns. Suitable fluorinated resin yarns may include, for example, polytetrafluoroethylene or other fluoropolymer-based fibers. The accompanying yarns may be selected according to the intended application and may include fibers with high strength, high temperature resistance, or good bonding properties. When woven into a fabric, the fluorinated resin yarns are exposed at or near the working surface so that they can provide continuous self-lubricating performance during sliding contact. At the same time, the non-fluorinated yarns contribute to the integrity of the fabric and improve its ability to be laminated or bonded to a supporting substrate.

The fabric can be manufactured through a simple weaving process without the need for complicated post-treatment, external lubricants, or pollution-generating coating operations. Because the lubricating component is incorporated directly into the yarn structure, the fabric maintains stable performance over long periods of use. The specified relationship between the yarn surface areas and diameters helps ensure that the fluorinated resin is present in an amount sufficient to reduce friction, while avoiding excessive weakening of the fabric or poor bonding strength.

The resulting self-lubricating fabric exhibits a low friction coefficient, excellent abrasion and wear resistance, high laminating strength, and good reliability under demanding operating conditions. It is especially suitable for use in mechanical moving parts where conventional lubrication is difficult, undesirable, or ineffective. Examples include bearings, bushings, guide rails, sliding plates, hinges, and other components subject to repeated sliding or reciprocating motion.

Because of its combination of self-lubrication and mechanical strength, the fabric is particularly useful in low-speed and high-load environments, where ordinary lubricants may be squeezed out or may fail to form an effective lubricating film. It is also advantageous in extreme-temperature conditions, including high-temperature or low-temperature applications, where liquid lubricants may evaporate, degrade, freeze, or lose viscosity. In addition, the fabric can reduce maintenance requirements, avoid lubricant contamination, and improve the service life of mechanical assemblies.

Overall, the self-lubricating fabric provides a practical, low-cost, and environmentally friendly material for friction-reducing applications. Its production process is straightforward, its performance is durable, and its structure can be adjusted by selecting appropriate yarn materials and controlling their relative surface-area and diameter ratios. As a result, it offers an effective solution for mechanical systems requiring reliable lubrication, strong bonding performance, and long-term wear resistance under severe working conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a self-lubricating fabric made from composite yarns containing fluorinated resin yarns, including its structure, manufacturing method, advantages, and applications in mechanical moving parts.
counterfactuals.output:
A self-lubricating fabric for mechanical moving parts is disclosed. The fabric is woven, knitted, braided, or otherwise formed from composite yarns comprising at least one fluorinated resin yarn and at least one reinforcing or supporting fiber yarn. The fluorinated resin yarn may include polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), modified PTFE, fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP), perfluoroalkoxy resin (PFA), ethylene-tetrafluoroethylene (ETFE), or combinations thereof, and is arranged so as to be exposed at least partially on a frictional contact surface of the fabric. The reinforcing yarn may include glass fiber, aramid fiber, carbon fiber, polyester fiber, polyimide fiber, metal fiber, or mixtures thereof, thereby providing dimensional stability, tensile strength, heat resistance, and load-bearing capacity.

The fabric is manufactured by forming the composite yarn through twisting, covering, commingling, wrapping, or air-jet interlacing of the fluorinated resin yarn with the reinforcing yarn, followed by weaving or knitting the composite yarn into a predetermined fabric structure. The fabric may further be subjected to heat setting, calendering, impregnation with a binder resin, lamination to a backing layer, or surface finishing to improve bonding strength, wear resistance, and frictional performance.

The resulting fabric provides a low coefficient of friction without the need for external lubricating oil or grease, exhibits excellent wear resistance, chemical resistance, heat resistance, and anti-adhesion properties, and reduces noise, vibration, and maintenance requirements during operation. The fabric is suitable for use as a sliding liner, bearing liner, bushing material, guide rail liner, seal support, conveyor sliding surface, hinge interface, piston or actuator guide, and other friction-reducing components in mechanical moving parts, particularly where clean, dry, or maintenance-free operation is required.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention of a low-friction self-lubricating fabric where warp or weft yarns are composite fluorinated resin yarns and other yarns, with surface area and diameter ratio limitations.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a woven, low-friction self-lubricating fabric intended for sliding or bearing applications.

It uses a fabric structure in which at least one yarn system—warp or weft—includes:

- **Composite fluorinated resin yarns**, such as PTFE-containing yarns, which provide the low-friction/self-lubricating sliding surface; and  
- **Other yarns**, typically stronger or more wear-resistant reinforcing yarns, which give the fabric mechanical strength, dimensional stability, and durability.

The key feature is that the fabric is not merely a random mixture of PTFE and reinforcing fibers. Instead, the construction is controlled by limits on:

1. **Surface area ratio** — the exposed area of the composite fluorinated resin yarns on the fabric surface must fall within a defined range so that enough fluorinated resin is present to provide lubrication, but not so much that strength and wear resistance are sacrificed.

2. **Yarn diameter ratio** — the diameter of the composite fluorinated resin yarns relative to the other yarns is also limited so that the fluorinated yarns are properly exposed at the sliding surface while the other yarns still support the structure.

In essence, the invention balances **low friction**, **self-lubrication**, **load-bearing strength**, and **wear resistance** by controlling both the amount of fluorinated resin yarn visible on the surface and the relative yarn sizes in the woven fabric.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent claim summary for a self-lubricating textile suitable for low-speed, high-load, high- or low-temperature mechanical applications, including composition, performance characteristics, and uses.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent Claim Summary: Self-Lubricating Textile for Low-Speed, High-Load Mechanical Applications

### 1. Claimed Article

A self-lubricating textile material configured for use in mechanical systems operating under low-speed, high-load conditions, including environments subject to elevated or cryogenic temperatures. The textile provides inherent lubrication, wear resistance, and dimensional stability without requiring continuous external lubricant supply.

### 2. Composition

The textile comprises a woven, braided, knitted, nonwoven, or composite fibrous structure including:

- **High-strength load-bearing fibers**, such as aramid fibers, carbon fibers, glass fibers, basalt fibers, polyimide fibers, polybenzoxazole fibers, ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene fibers, or combinations thereof.
- **Low-friction or self-lubricating fibers or particles**, such as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), modified fluoropolymers, graphite, molybdenum disulfide, boron nitride, graphene, fluorinated ethylene propylene, perfluoroalkoxy polymers, or combinations thereof.
- **Thermally stable matrix or binder material**, optionally including polyimide, phenolic resin, epoxy resin, silicone resin, fluoropolymer binder, ceramic precursor, or other high-temperature polymeric or inorganic binders.
- **Optional reinforcement or surface treatment**, including metallic coatings, ceramic coatings, plasma treatment, impregnation with solid lubricant particles, or resin impregnation to improve durability, adhesion, compressive strength, or temperature resistance.

In certain embodiments, the textile includes a hybrid yarn structure in which load-bearing fibers are combined with self-lubricating fibers, or a layered construction having a high-strength backing layer and a low-friction wear surface.

### 3. Performance Characteristics

The self-lubricating textile is characterized by one or more of the following properties:

- Low coefficient of friction under low-speed, high-load sliding or oscillating contact.
- High wear resistance under boundary-lubricated or dry-running conditions.
- Capability to operate under high contact pressures and compressive loads.
- Stable performance at elevated temperatures, for example above 150°C, 250°C, or 300°C depending on fiber and binder selection.
- Stable performance at low or cryogenic temperatures, including temperatures below −40°C, −100°C, or −150°C.
- Resistance to seizure, galling, stick-slip motion, and lubricant starvation.
- Chemical resistance to oils, fuels, hydraulic fluids, solvents, water, salt spray, or corrosive atmospheres.
- Dimensional stability and low creep under sustained mechanical loading.
- Reduced maintenance requirements compared with grease-lubricated or oil-lubricated bearing materials.

### 4. Representative Uses

The textile is suitable for incorporation into or use as:

- Plain bearings, sleeve bearings, journal bearings, thrust washers, and bushings.
- Sliding pads, wear liners, guide rails, spherical bearing liners, and hinge liners.
- Seals, packing materials, gasket interfaces, and dynamic sealing elements.
- Aerospace mechanisms, including landing gear components, flap tracks, actuator bearings, control surface hinges, and space mechanisms.
- Automotive, rail, marine, industrial, mining, and heavy equipment components exposed to high loads and intermittent motion.
- Cryogenic valves, pumps, couplings, and mechanisms used in liquefied gas handling.
- High-temperature machinery, furnace equipment, turbines, engine-adjacent components, and industrial processing equipment.

### 5. Functional Claim Concept

The claimed textile provides a load-supporting fibrous architecture combined with an integrated solid-lubricant phase, such that lubrication is supplied by the textile itself during sliding contact. The textile maintains low friction and wear resistance across a broad temperature range and under high mechanical loads, thereby enabling dry-running or minimally lubricated operation in demanding mechanical applications.

### 6. Example Independent Claim-Style Summary

A self-lubricating textile for mechanical bearing or sliding applications, comprising a fibrous textile structure including load-bearing reinforcement fibers and a solid-lubricant component distributed within, on, or among the fibers, wherein the textile is configured to withstand high compressive loading and low-speed sliding contact while providing a low-friction wear surface without continuous external lubrication, and wherein the textile retains lubricating and wear-resistant performance at elevated or sub-ambient temperatures.

### 7. Example Dependent Claim Features

The textile may further be characterized in that:

1. The reinforcement fibers comprise aramid, carbon, glass, polyimide, ceramic, or mixtures thereof.  
2. The solid-lubricant component comprises PTFE, graphite, molybdenum disulfide, boron nitride, graphene, or combinations thereof.  
3. The textile is impregnated with a thermally stable resin or binder.  
4. The textile comprises a woven structure having a lubricating face and a load-bearing backing.  
5. The textile is bonded to a metallic, polymeric, ceramic, or composite substrate.  
6. The textile is configured as a bearing liner, bushing liner, thrust washer, sliding pad, seal, or wear strip.  
7. The textile operates under dry-running, intermittent lubrication, or lubricant-starved conditions.  
8. The textile maintains low friction and wear resistance at temperatures above 200°C or below −100°C.  
9. The textile resists creep, extrusion, and delamination under high bearing pressure.  
10. The textile reduces maintenance and lubricant requirements in heavy-duty mechanical systems.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
